title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 1-dimensional 'géométrie des formes' without points or topology given in advance. There is a set L of 'lieux' and a set S of 'segments'. Each I in S has a support Ĩ ⊂ L and a boundary ∂I = {x,y}, a 2-element subset of Ĩ. The interior is Ĩ° = Ĩ \ ∂I. Sub-segments I_{x,u} are given by F1/F2. Cor. 4 on the previous page says Ĩ determines I, so S can be viewed as a set of subsets of L. F3 is a germ-dichotomy at a common endpoint x: two segments I, J with x in ∂I ∩ ∂J either share an initial piece, or have initial pieces meeting only in x. This gives an equivalence relation R_x on S_x = {I : x ∈ ∂I}. The quotient B_x = S_x/R_x is the set of branches at x, and its cardinality is the order of x.

This page: (1) Terminology. Order 0 is an isolated lieu; order 1 is a 'lieu-bout' (endpoint); the order is assumed or required to be finite. (2) A lieu x is regular if x ∈ Ĩ° for some segment I. L_r = ∪_{I∈S} Ĩ° and L_s = L \ L_r are the singular lieux. These are presumably the isolated points, the endpoints and the branch points. (3) Axiom F4, gluing. Let I', I'' ∈ S with Ĩ' ∩ Ĩ'' = ∂I' ∩ ∂I'' = {z}, z regular, ∂I' = {x,z}, ∂I'' = {y,z}. Then there is a unique I ∈ S with Ĩ ⊃ Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ'' (Grothendieck adds that in fact equality holds) and ∂I = {x,y}. In F1 notation, I' = I_{x,z} and I'' = I_{y,z}. The margin calls this an axiom of joining two pieces. (4) Cor. 1, extension of a segment beyond a regular endpoint. If I ∈ S, ∂I = {x,y} and x is regular, there is J ∈ S with J̃ ⊃ Ĩ, ∂J = {y',y}, y' ≠ x, so that ∂J ∩ ∂I = {y} and x ∈ J̃°. Proof sketch: since x is interior to some segment, F1/F2 give two sub-segments ending at x in different branches, so the order of x is ≥ 2. F3 then yields K with K̃ ∩ Ĩ = ∂K ∩ ∂I = {x}, and F4 glues K and I. The next page continues with Cor. 2 (a segment with regular endpoints lies in the interior of a larger one) and F5 (regular lieux have order exactly 2, equivalently the interiors of segments through x form a filter base).

Purpose: to axiomatize tame 1-dimensional 'shapes', i.e. graphs and 1-manifolds with stratification, combinatorially via segments, as a first step of the 'géométrie des formes' related to the tame-topology programme. Regular points form the 1-dimensional open stratum; singular points are the vertices.
errors: Gap in the proof sketch of Cor. 1. F3 only gives sub-segments K = K_{x,v} and I_{x,u} with K̃ ∩ Ĩ_{x,u} = {x}. It does not give K̃ ∩ Ĩ = {x} for the whole of I: K could meet Ĩ_{u,y}, e.g. near a loop. A further shrinking argument is needed to choose v so that K̃_{x,v} avoids all of Ĩ, and the axioms F1–F4 stated so far do not obviously provide one. Grothendieck's own margin on the previous page ('Il manque ... partie (b) de F3', F3') suggests he was aware F3 needed strengthening.

The definition of regular lieu (interior of some segment), combined with F5 (regular lieux have order 2), forces segments never to pass through branch points. In the model where L is a graph and S is all arcs, a vertex of degree 3 would be regular of order 3. So S must be a restricted family, such as sub-arcs of edges. This is implicit, not stated on the page.
Uniqueness in F4 relies on Cor. 4 (Ĩ determines I) together with the parenthetical claim Ĩ = Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ''. The latter is asserted ('par égalité !') rather than derived.

ideas.what: Order of a lieu as the number of branches (germ classes of segments) at it; order 0 = isolated, order 1 = endpoint
ideas.modern_name: Menger–Urysohn order / branching number; valence of a vertex in a graph

ideas.what: Regular vs singular lieux: regular = interior of a segment; singular = complement
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of a 1-dimensional polyhedron/graph into open edges and vertices

ideas.what: Axiom F4: two segments meeting only in a common regular endpoint glue uniquely to a segment whose support is their union
ideas.modern_name: Concatenation/gluing axiom of arcs; betweenness-style axiom (Pasch/Hilbert ordered geometry analogue)
ideas.usually_credited_to: axiomatic ordered geometry (Pasch, Hilbert, Veblen) in spirit

ideas.what: Cor. 1: a segment can be prolonged beyond a regular endpoint
ideas.modern_name: Extendability of arcs at manifold points (no-boundary property)

ideas.what: Overall programme: point-set-free axiomatics of 1-dimensional tame shapes via a set of 'lieux' and a family of 'segments' with support and boundary maps
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/combinatorial tame topology; cf. o-minimal 1-dimensional cell structures, betweenness/arc systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality); Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches tame topology in general terms, not this segment axiomatics

missed.claim: An abandoned axiomatic system (F1–F5) for 1-dimensional 'formes' based on lieux and segments with support/boundary maps, branches and order. It is a combinatorial, topology-free characterization of tame graphs/1-manifolds that was never completed or published.
missed.quote: Soient I', I'' ∈ S, z ∈ L, tels que Ĩ' ∩ Ĩ'' = ∂I' ∩ ∂I'' = {z}, avec z régulier ... ∃! I ∈ S tel que Ĩ ⊃ Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ''
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to start the 'géométrie des formes' / tame topology programme: dimension 1 first, via an arc system rather than o-minimal structures. Comparing it with o-minimal 1-dimensional cell decomposition or with axiomatic betweenness theories could be of historical interest. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary 1-dimensional topology (order of points, regular vs singular points, gluing and extension of arcs) recast axiomatically. It is historically interesting as the beginning of the unpublished 'géométrie des formes' axiomatics, but contains no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '(on simplifie par égalité !)' more likely reads '(ou plutôt égalité !)', meaning Ĩ = Ĩ' ∪ Ĩ''. This fits the mathematics.
'[dans un cadre de F1, ...]' likely reads '[dans les notations de F1, I' = I_{x,z}, I'' = I_{y,z}]'.
'lieux singuliers, ce sont ceux, ou des bouts directement' is uncertain. It probably lists the kinds of singular lieux (isolated points, endpoints, branch points); the exact words are illegible.
The left-margin note by F4 is uncertain; 'Axiome de raccordement de deux portions' is possible instead of 'recollement de deux parties'.
The first line presumably continues the previous page: 'ordre 0 : lieu isolé, ordre 1 : lieu-bout'.
The page carries '6' at the top and '7' at the bottom left (archive/own numbering).
